_about: The watcher's configuration (pipeline/watch.py). Each adapter runs when its every_days have passed since a source was last checked. The denylist is never fetched, even when a record cites it: Play pages of any kind (owner captures them by hand), CanLII (its terms bar systematic downloading) and Exodus (CLAUDE.md, Exodus etiquette).

quote_drift._about: Every page a reviewed record quotes (pipeline/watch_quotes.py). These are pages FinePrint already quotes under its 15-word rule. sources gives a page its own settings: max_bytes raises the 5 MB cap for that page only.

https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1._about: The e-Evidence Regulation's page is over 5 MB.

https://advocacy.consumerreports.org/wp-._about: Consumer Reports' study, a PDF over 5 MB.

rss._about: Regulators' feeds (pipeline/watch_rss.py): an entry naming a recorded company, app or tracker becomes a new_event. Entries older than max_age_days are skipped.

feeds.name: OPC: Investigations into businesses
feeds._about: Findings under PIPEDA. FinePrint already quotes OPC pages under its 15-word rule.

feeds.name: BC OIPC: Rulings and Reports
feeds._about: Orders, decisions and investigation reports. Its terms of reuse haven't been checked, so its entries are leads for now.

_not_watched.name: FTC press releases: consumer protection
_not_watched.why: On 2026-10-08 ftc.gov answered the watcher's robots.txt request with a block page (it said the request resembled an abusive automated request), which counts as disallowing everything. A refusal is a refusal: not watched.
